newsitem.title: USA: Russia made scant progress on rights, U.S. says.
newsitem.headline: Russia made scant progress on rights, U.S. says.

text.p: Russia's human rights record showed little progress last year, with Russian forces using "indiscriminate and disproportionate" force in the breakaway Republic of Chechnya, the United States said on Thursday.

"Domestic and foreign human rights groups continued to document serious violations of international humanitarian law and human rights in the Republic of Chechnya," the State Department said in its human rights survey. "Violations committed by Russian forces continued to occur on a much larger scale than those of the Chechen rebels."
"Russian forces engaged in the indiscrimate and disproportionate use of force, resulting in numerous civilian deaths," the annual worldwide survey said.
It said Russian forces had prevented civilians from evacuating areas of imminent danger and blocked humanitarian groups from helping needy civilians.
These actions were in conflict with a number of Russia's international obligations, the State Department said.
It said tens of thousands of civilians have been killed and more than 500,000 people have been displaced since the conflict began in December 1994.
